title: Represent apparatus, crews, and GPS devices

scenes.title: Represent apparatus, crews, and GPS devices
scenes.narration: Welcome to Resgrid Academy. In this lesson, we will represent apparatus, crews, and gps devices. A vehicle name alone does not tell a dispatcher its type, home station, crew, or location source. We will explain the features, the setup decisions, and a practical way to check the result.

scenes.title: A department scenario
scenes.narration: Engine 1 and Rescue 1 are added with their unit types and assigned to Station 1. Units let dispatchers send the right resources and let everyone see which apparatus is available. The examples in this series use a fictional department and are teaching scenarios, not default settings.

scenes.title: Units
scenes.narration: Units. Your apparatus, vehicles and response teams. Add each unit with its type and home station group.

scenes.title: Unit types
scenes.narration: Unit types. Categories such as Engine, Ladder or Ambulance. Create unit types before adding units so each unit can be classified.

scenes.title: Hardware location tracking
scenes.narration: Hardware location tracking. GPS devices that report unit locations. Register each tracking device and link it to its unit.

scenes.title: New Unit
scenes.narration: New Unit. Add an apparatus, vehicle or team. List your apparatus or response teams with their types and home stations. Teams that respond only as individuals can mark this module not applicable.

scenes.title: Unit Staffing
scenes.narration: Unit Staffing. Assign crew members to units. List your apparatus or response teams with their types and home stations. Teams that respond only as individuals can mark this module not applicable.

scenes.title: Configure one useful workflow
scenes.narration: For the training scenario, work in this order. Step 1. Create Engine and Rescue unit types. Step 2. Add Engine 1 with its type, Station 1, and crew roles. Step 3. Assign the crew and, when used, register a tracking device against the unit.

scenes.title: Verify the result
scenes.narration: Now verify the result. Confirm the unit type, home station, crew, and status. For hardware tracking, check a recent received position and the stale-position behavior. A common problem to watch for: An old GPS position is not a live position. Crew assignment, reported unit status, and physical readiness are distinct.

scenes.title: Try it with your department
scenes.narration: Your practice task is simple. Create Engine 1 in the demo department and verify the assigned crew from the dispatcher view. Measure incomplete unit records. Record the result, who owns the follow-up, and when it should be reviewed.
